fields.name: Hita Harivaṁśa
fields.place: Gauḍa (born); Bādgrām near Mathurā; Vṛndāvana (Rādhāvallabhajī, Rāsa-maṇḍala at Govinda-ghāṭ, Nikuñja-vana)
fields.guru: Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, who disowned him (Prema-vilāsa 18)
fields.notes: Founder of the Rādhāvallabha sampradāya; son of Vyāsa Miśra and Tārā-devī; installed Śrī Rādhāvallabhajī in Vṛndāvana in 1508. First a disciple of Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, who disowned him for taking Rādhā's betel prasāda on a Harivāsara (Prema-vilāsa 18). Died 1551.

fields.name: Oṛiyā woman who climbed the Garuḍa column
fields.notes: A woman of Orissa who, to see Jagannātha over the crowd, climbed the Garuḍa-stambha with her foot on Lord Caitanya's shoulder; the Lord stopped Govinda from pulling her down and prayed for her eagerness (CC Antya 14.22-30).

Court poet of King Śivasiṁha of Mithilā (some think a Bengali); his songs, naming Śivasiṁha and Queen Lachimā, were relished by Lord Caitanya in the Gambhīrā. Contemporary of Caṇḍīdāsa (#1813). Also wrote the Puruṣa-parīkṣā, Kīrtilatā, Gorakṣa-vijaya (before 1416) and other works.
